Feature: Independent control register for each GPIO
Test Description: Verify that per-pin and group GPIO control and data/status registers reset to their expected values and that masked write/read operations produce the expected readback across multiple patterns.
Remarks: When reading default values without actively driving inputs, input status can read high; forcing a low level may assert internal selection and cause a mismatch during default-value checks.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Start the test case execution.
2) For each per-pin and group register in the list that is readable and not excluded from reset checks, read the register and compare the value against the documented default; count a failure on mismatch.
3) For each data pattern, for each address that is writable and not excluded, write the pattern masked by the register's write mask.
4) For each address that is both writable and readable and not excluded, read the register, then compare against the expected value computed from the written data, the read mask, the write mask, and preserved default bits; count a failure on mismatch.
5) Finish with pass if no default mismatches and no write-read mismatches; otherwise fail.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria: 1) For each readable register not excluded from reset checks, the value must equal the documented default.\n2) For each writable and readable register, after writing masked data, the read value must equal the expected masked combination of the written data and the preserved default bits.\n3) Overall pass when both the default-mismatch counter and the write-read-mismatch counter are zero.

Test Description: Validate that configuring per-pin control for input mode with negative-edge interrupt enables produces an interrupt per pin; confirm masked group status, then clear per-pin and group status; confirm system interrupt routing and clear.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance.
2) Enable the GPIO interrupt path in the system interrupt enable register for the selected GPIO instance.
3) Drive the external stimulus high to establish a known starting level.
4) For each pin from 8 to 39, program the per-pin control to input mode, enable negative-edge detection, and clear any latched raw status; wait for a short delay after each configuration.
5) For each pin, pre-clear the corresponding bit in the raw status/clear register.
6) Enable the group interrupt for only the current pin and wait briefly.
7) Arm the pending-interrupt flag, then produce a falling edge on the selected pin by toggling the external stimulus from high to low; wait with a bounded timeout until the interrupt is observed.
8) In the interrupt service, verify the per-pin input indicates low, check that the masked group status shows the active pin, then clear the per-pin raw status and the group raw bit; verify the masked group status reads zero.
9) Clear the system raw interrupt status for the selected GPIO instance and acknowledge the interrupt at the controller.
10) Repeat for all pins and report the final error count.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1) For each pin, an interrupt must be observed before the timeout expires.
2) In the service routine, the per-pin input must indicate low after the falling edge.
3) The masked group status must indicate the active pin during service and must read zero after clearing both per-pin and group status.
4) The system raw status must clear successfully.
5) Overall pass when the final reported error count is zero.

Test Description: Validate that enabling positive-edge detection on all GPIO pins and enabling the group interrupt produces a group interrupt on a rising edge per pin; confirm masked group status, successful per-pin raw clear, and successful system raw clear; verify no timeouts.
Test Steps / Procedure:
1) Enable the platform interrupt for the selected GPIO instance.
2) Enable the GPIO interrupt path in the system interrupt enable register for the selected GPIO instance.
3) For each pin from 8 to 39, write the per-pin control to enable positive-edge detection.
4) Configure input mode for GPIOs 8–39 using the group IO control registers.
5) Enable the group interrupt for all pins.
6) For each pin, drive the stimulus low, arm the wait, then generate a rising edge; wait with a timeout for the interrupt to arrive.
7) In the interrupt service, read the masked group status; if non-zero, proceed, else record an error.
8) Clear per-pin raw status across all pins and verify the masked group status reads zero.
9) Clear the system raw interrupt status and verify it is cleared; re-enable the group interrupt and acknowledge the interrupt.
10) Complete all pins and report the accumulated error count.
Validation / Acceptance Criteria:
1) For each pin, an interrupt must be observed before the timeout expires.
2) During service, masked group status must indicate an active condition and must read zero after the per-pin clear sequence.
3) The system raw status must clear successfully.
4) Overall pass when the final reported error count is zero.
